sections.abstract: The paper introduces SLAM3R, a novel end-to-end system for real-time, high-quality dense 3D reconstruction from monocular RGB videos. By integrating local 3D reconstruction and global coordinate registration through feed-forward neural networks, SLAM3R processes video into overlapping clips via a sliding window. Unlike traditional methods, it directly regresses 3D pointmaps and progressively aligns them to create globally consistent scenes without explicit camera parameter estimation or costly optimization, achieving state-of-the-art performance at 20+ FPS.
sections.introduction: Dense 3D reconstruction remains a challenge, with traditional pipelines (SfM/MVS) often requiring offline processing and recent dense SLAM systems suffering from low efficiency. SLAM3R addresses these gaps using a two-hierarchy framework: first, reconstructing local geometry from sliding windows, and second, registering these into a global scene. The system utilizes Image-to-Points (I2P) and Local-to-World (L2W) networks to enable efficient reconstruction. Key contributions include the end-to-end architecture, novel multi-view I2P and L2W modules, and superior performance on public benchmarks.
sections.method:
SLAM3R builds on end-to-end foundations like DUSt3R to reconstruct a dense pointcloud $P \in \mathbb{R}^{M \times 3}$ from RGB frames $\{I_i \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times 3}\}_{i=1}^N$ using sliding windows $W_i$ of length $L$.

**Inner-Window Local Reconstruction (I2P):** This module uses a ViT backbone with a shared encoder $E_{img}$ and decoders $D_{key}, D_{sup}$. Encoder: $F_i^{(T \times d)} = E_{img}(I_i^{(H \times W \times 3)}), i=1, ..., L$. Keyframe decoder: $G_{key} = D_{key}(F_{key}, F_{sup_1}, ..., F_{sup_{L-1}})$. Supporting decoder: $G_{sup_i} = D_{sup}(F_{sup_i}, F_{key})$. Pointmaps $\hat{X}_i$ and confidence $\hat{C}_i$ are predicted via head H: $\hat{X}_i^{(H \times W \times 3)}, \hat{C}_i^{(H \times W \times 1)} = \text{H}(G_i^{(T \times d)})$. Loss: $\mathcal{L}_{I2P} = \sum_{i=1}^L M_i \cdot ( \hat{C}_i \cdot \text{L1}(\frac{1}{\hat{z}}\hat{X}_i, \frac{1}{z}X_i) - \alpha \log \hat{C}_i )$.

**Inter-Window Global Registration (L2W):** This module registers local maps into global coordinates using a reservoir strategy and retrieval module. Geometric tokens: $\mathcal{P}_i^{(T \times d)} = E_{pts}(\hat{X}_i^{(H \times W \times 3)})$. Combined tokens: $\mathcal{F}_i^{(T \times d)} = F_i^{(T \times d)} + \mathcal{P}_i^{(T \times d)}$. Registration decoder: $\mathcal{G}_{key} = D_{reg}(\mathcal{F}_{key}, \mathcal{F}_{sce_1}, ..., \mathcal{F}_{sce_{K}})$. Scene decoder: $\mathcal{G}_{sce_i} = D_{sce}(\mathcal{F}_{sce_i}, \mathcal{F}_{key})$. Loss: $\mathcal{L}_{L2W} = \sum_{i=1}^L M_i \cdot ( \tilde{C}_i \cdot \text{L1}(\tilde{X}_i, X_i) - \alpha \log \tilde{C}_i )$.
sections.experiments: Models are trained on ~850K clips from ScanNet++, Aria Synthetic Environments, and CO3D-v2. Evaluation is conducted on 7 Scenes and Replica datasets. The architecture uses DUSt3R initialization with $m=24$ encoder and $n=12$ decoder blocks. Training was performed on 8 NVIDIA 4090D GPUs. Implementation details include specific frame sampling and stride settings for different datasets, such as $Skip=20, K=10$ for Replica and stride 20, $K=5$ for 7 Scenes.
sections.results: SLAM3R outperforms baselines like DUSt3R, MASt3R, and Spann3R on the 7 Scenes dataset in accuracy and completeness while maintaining ~25 FPS. On Replica, it achieves quality comparable to optimization-based methods like NICER-SLAM. Camera pose results (ATE-RMSE) show competitive performance with minimal drift. Ablations confirm that a window size of $L=11$ is optimal, the retrieval module significantly improves performance over nearest-neighbor selection, and the L2W module is more effective than traditional alignment methods (ICP/Umeyama). The system also demonstrates strong generalization on in-the-wild videos and benchmarks like Tanks and Temples and ETH3D.
sections.conclusion: SLAM3R provides a real-time, high-quality dense 3D reconstruction solution using a two-hierarchy neural framework that eliminates explicit camera parameter estimation. While achieving state-of-the-art results at 20+ FPS, limitations include the lack of global bundle adjustment and pose accuracy that still falls short of specialized localization systems. Future work will focus on addressing these constraints.
sections.supplementary: Supplementary material details the retrieval module loss: $\mathcal{L}_{Retr} = \sum_{i=1}^{R} |S_i' - Mean(C_i')|$, where $S_i' = Sigmoid(S_i)$ and $C_i' = (C_i - 1)/C_i$. It describes multi-keyframe co-registration and training schedules (100 epochs for I2P, 200 for L2W). Evaluation metrics are defined: $Accuracy = \frac{1}{P} \sum_{i=1}^P \min_j (D(x_i, y_j))$, $Completeness = \frac{1}{Q} \sum_{j=1}^Q \min_i (D(x_i, y_j))$, and $ATE-RMSE = \sqrt{\frac{1}{F} \sum_{i=1}^F D(T_i^{gt}, T_i^{perd})^2}$. Additional results on ScanNet, Tanks and Temples, and DTU further verify the system's low drift and high-quality dense point cloud generation.
